# Ray-Volume and Bounding Box Intersection

Also called: Ray-Box Intersection, AABB Intersection, Slab Method, Face Distance Method

## Overview
This family provides the geometric primitives for determining the entry and exit points of a viewing ray relative to a volume's spatial bounds, which is the prerequisite for volume traversal and sampling. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by focusing on axis-aligned or planar volume boundaries rather than general triangles or implicit surfaces, providing the specific $[t_{near}, t_{far}]$ intervals required for marching algorithms.

## Shared principles
The shared principles of this family are the geometric definition of rays and the parallel execution model [G].
**Ray Definition**
Rays are defined by an origin $\mathbf{o}$ and a direction $\mathbf{d}$ [G]. The direction is typically normalized. The origin is often the camera eye position, but can vary based on the camera model [G].
**Parallel Execution**
Computations are mapped to parallel threads [G]. Each thread typically processes one or more pixels or samples [G]. Memory access patterns are optimized for coalescing [G]. Synchronization is used to manage data dependencies between threads [G].

## Subtopics

### [Ray-box intersection](776-ray-box-intersection.md)
Computes the parametric entry ($t_{near}$) and exit ($t_{far}$) distances of a ray intersecting an Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB). It solves the problem of determining the valid sampling interval along a ray for volume rendering, ensuring that density or color sampling occurs only within the volume's physical bounds. Unlike [Ray-box intersection via OpenGL Geometry Shaders](1768-ray-box-intersection-via-opengl-geometry-shaders.md) which rasterizes the box to derive intersection data, this method performs an analytical calculation. It sets itself apart from [Ray-AABB Intersection (Slab/Min-Max)](6548-ray-aabb-intersection-slab-min-max.md) by explicitly providing the scalar interval $[t_{min}, t_{max}]$ required for subsequent [volume sampling](#7111-volume-sampling.md) or traversal, rather than just a boolean hit test [G].

### [Ray-Volume Intersection (Face Distance Method)](2381-ray-volume-intersection-face-distance-method.md)
A two-step procedure to determine if a viewing ray intersects the data volume and to find the entry point for volume traversal. It calculates distances from the ray origin to each of the six faces of the volume geometry, divides by the corresponding ray direction component, and selects the smallest valid distance as the nearest impact point.

### [Ray Filtering](2681-ray-filtering.md)
Reduces computational load by discarding rays that do not intersect with the scene's geometry or alpha mask before expensive volume rendering steps. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods by operating as a pre-processing culling stage on a batch of rays, often integrating alpha-mask density checks alongside axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) intersection tests.

### [Procedural Ray/Box Intersection](8356-procedural-ray-box-intersection.md)
Determines ray entry and exit within a volume's bounding box entirely within the fragment shader, without pre-rendering geometry. It computes the ray's intersection with the bounding box directly in the shader, allowing the volume to be rendered as a simple screen-aligned quad or similar primitive. Unlike rasterization-based setup methods that use geometry to pass ray data, this approach is self-contained but places the full computational load of intersection and marching on the fragment shader.

### Clipping Cell-Level Slice to Active Rays
An optimization to reduce cell primitives in a slice by intersecting individual rays with the world-space bounding box of the current u,v slice [S1, unofficial]. Rays that have already successfully hit a cell are considered "inactive" and are ignored, even if they intersect the slice bounding box [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The slab method for AABB intersection is a standard technique in ray tracing, widely cited in foundational graphics literature [S2, S3, S4, S6, S16, S22, S25, S30, S34, S43, S46, S53, unofficial][S56][S57, unofficial]. The face distance method appears in early interactive volume rendering contexts [S1, unofficial]. [Ray filtering](#2681-ray-filtering.md) techniques are employed in modern GPU-based volume renderers to optimize batch processing [S1, S2, unofficial]. Procedural intersection in shaders is used in real-time rendering to avoid geometry overhead [S1, S2, unofficial].
